svg.title: What can earn a Generalizability 5 versus what stays capped near 3
svg.desc: Illustrative two-column figure for the Generalizability axis. The left green column, headed "Can reach 5 (a real external dataset backs it)", holds two cards. Card one: PD variability is backed by PhysioNet Gait-in-PD (gaitpdb, DOI 10.13026/C24H3N), which is force-plate and IMU data, not skeletons, so it confirms the biomarker at the label level (cross-modal, not a BlazePose skeleton transfer). Card two: cross-view invariance is backed by CASIA-B, OU-MVLP-Pose, GREW, and Gait3D, which are large, non-clinical, multi-view pose cohorts. The right amber column, headed "Capped near 3 (no matching external skeleton dataset exists)", holds one card: cerebral-palsy-specific and myopathy-specific claims have no participant-disjoint public skeleton cohort, so each stays an internal, transductive result. All numbers are transductive; folder labels are dataset annotations, not diagnoses.
svg.text: What earns a Generalizability 5, and what is capped near 3
The rubric only lets a claim reach 5 when a real external cohort backs it. With no matching external skeleton cohort, a claim stays near 3. All numbers transductive.
Can reach 5 (a real external dataset backs it)
PD variability
PhysioNet Gait-in-PD (gaitpdb)
Force-plate and IMU data, not skeletons, so it confirms the
variability biomarker at the label level (cross-modal), not a
BlazePose skeleton transfer. DOI 10.13026/C24H3N.
Cross-view invariance
CASIA-B, OU-MVLP-Pose, GREW, Gait3D
Large, non-clinical, multi-view pose cohorts. A skeleton can
be tested on people it never saw, from angles it never saw,
so the claim can transfer beyond the tiny internal cohort.
Capped near 3 (no matching
external skeleton dataset exists)
Cerebral-palsy-specific and
myopathy-specific claims
No participant-disjoint skeleton cohort
No public skeleton dataset exists with different people for
either condition. There is nothing external to test on, so
the result cannot leave the training set.
It stays an internal, transductive result: the frozen encoder
already saw every clip it is scored on, so the score shows
separability on seen data, not transfer to new people.
This honest limit is stated on every relevant item. The
neuroscience defines the target, it does not lift the ceiling.
Illustrative. All numbers transductive. Folder labels are dataset annotations, not diagnoses. Rubric: Generalizability weight 0.25; a 5 needs a real external cohort.
